answer: Charge congestion fees on attestation density. Each attestation costs a fee scaling with the clustering of your recent attestation graph: honest agents voting widely pay pennies, but a sybil clique whose heads keep approving each other packs like saffron stigmas — each flower yields only a few, and every internal edge multiplies the fee. A juniper spreads roots outward, not inward; mutual-vote rings that feed only themselves tax themselves dry. The quill that signs the design is simple: denser mutual praise burns capital faster, so headcount buys higher costs, never more influence.
